chunks.text: AIP Advances ARTICLE scitation.org/journal/adv Fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance for hydraulic system based on digital twin model Cite as: AIP Advances 12, 065213 (2022); doi: 10.1063/5.0098632 Submitted: 11 May 2022 • Accepted: 27 May 2022 • Published Online: 16 June 2022 Lintao Wang,a) Yuchong Liu,b) Hang Yin,c) and Wei Sund) AFFILIATIONS School of Mechanical Engineering, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian, China a)Author to whom correspondence should be addressed: wlt@dlut.edu.cn b)lyccc@mail.dlut.edu.cn c)32004085@mail.dlut.edu.cn d)sunwei@dlut.edu.cn ABSTRACT Hydraulic system has been the mainstream choice in large engineering equipment due to its smooth transmission, large bearing capacity, and small volume. However, because of the tightness and invisibility in hydraulic equipment, it is difficult to check and predict its faults. Common fault diagnosis and maintenance methods for the hydraulic system can be divided into two types: a signal analysis based on the mathematical model and a machine learning algorithm based on artificial intelligence. The first method can only diagnose specific faults based on the mathematical model, which is not universal, and the second one must rely on abundant history fault data, which is impossible to obtain in the early running stage. In order to address these questions, a digital twin framework is proposed which combines the virtual model with the real part to solve practical problems. As a concrete realization form of a five-dimension digital twin model, this framework provides a more feasible solution mode for fault diagnosis in the hydraulic system. Meanwhile, it expands the functions of faults prediction and digital model display. A case study of a hydraulic cylinder is used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The experimental result shows that this method can improve diagnosis accuracy for a hydraulic cylinder greatly compared with the non-interactive simulation model. Meanwhile, with the supplement of actual fault data, the diagnosis accuracy can be further improved, which has a certain growth ability and good applicability. © 2022 Author(s). INTRODUCTION As the prime transmission means used in large engineering equipment, the digitization and intelligence of the hydraulic trans- mission have become the basic link to realize the intelligent archi- tecture in the industry. On account of the tightness and invisibility of the hydraulic components, the faults that happened in the devices are not easy to check and remove.1,2 Therefore, it is difficult for users to make a reliable diagnosis for fault reasons and assessment for the remaining life of a hydraulic system. In view of this problem, traditional fault diagnosis methods can be divided into two basic directions: virtual model based and signal processing based.3,4 For the situation that it aims to detect several specific hydraulic faults and only has few historical fault data, the effective means is extracting the primary features based on signal processing technology and importing these data to the corresponding mathematical model for fault diagnosis. In view of this problem, traditional fault diagnosis methods can be divided into two basic directions: virtual model based and signal processing based.3,4 For the situation that it aims to detect several specific hydraulic faults and only has few historical fault data, the effective means is extracting the primary features based on signal processing technology and importing these data to the corresponding mathematical model for fault diagnosis. Goharrizi and Sepehri5 used the wavelet transform to analyze vibration signals and pressure signals of the hydraulic pump to achieve fault diag- nosis. These signal-based methods have been widely applied in the engineering field; however, for a complex system, it is difficult to establish a model according to the coupling between the variables. With the gradual realization of industrial digitization, the applica- tion of an artificial intelligence identification method as the main body combined with a variety of feature extraction means has made remarkable progress. Gareev et al.6 established a simulation model of the helicopter hydraulic system to construct datasets. By com- paring two methods including an SVM (Support Vector Machine) classifier based on linear, polynomial, and RBF (Radial Basis Func- tion) kernel and gradient enhancement based on a decision tree, a more suitable machine learning method is chosen for helicopter hydraulic system fault diagnosis. Since the feature data (features AIP Advances 12, 065213 (2022); doi: 10.1063/5.0098632 12, 065213-1 © Author(s) 2022 AIP Advances ARTICLE scitation.org/journal/adv extracted from the output curves of the system) for the training model all come from the initial simulation model, its validity can- not be guaranteed, and the final diagnosis accuracy is relatively low. Ji et al.7 greatly improved the accuracy of hydraulic valve fault detec- tion by integrating the multiple machine learning model to diagnose results by D-S (Dempster-Shafer) evidence theory and the informa- tion fusion method. This method can be applied to almost all basic hydraulic faults, which has high precision; nonetheless, they depend on abundant and effective history fault data, which is always unprac- tical in actual situations. According to the analysis above, these primary hydraulic fault detection methods all have some limitations in different circumstances. To overcome these restrictions, a more intelligent and compre- hensive solution framework should be proposed for the maintenance of the hydraulic system. According to different integration levels, the intelligent process in the industry has undergone three stages of upgrading.8 First is the virtual model stage that has no connec- tion with the physical entity. The second stage, digital shadow, only has a unidirectional connection between physical entities and virtual models. The latest version, digital twin, has a bidirectional con- nection between physical entities and virtual models in the device operation. The original concept of the digital twin was proposed by Professor Grieves9 in 2003 whose definition includes three parts: physical entity, virtual model, and their connection. industry has undergone three stages of upgrading.8 First is the virtual model stage that has no connec- tion with the physical entity. The second stage, digital shadow, only has a unidirectional connection between physical entities and virtual models. The latest version, digital twin, has a bidirectional con- nection between physical entities and virtual models in the device operation. The original concept of the digital twin was proposed by Professor Grieves9 in 2003 whose definition includes three parts: physical entity, virtual model, and their connection. Based on this frame, in order to achieve a more comprehensive acquisition of equipment information and expand its application capacity in life- cycle management, fault diagnosis, prediction, and other aspects, Tao et al.10,11 extended this framework to five dimensions that include a virtual model, a physical entity, an application function, twin data, and the connection between the four parts, which is more reasonable for the practical application of digital twin technology in the industry. In practical applications, the frequency of failure in the hydraulic system is very low and the types of faults are not com- prehensive, so it is difficult to generate sufficient historical data for the fault diagnosis model in the early or middle period of the equipment operation. Meanwhile, the fault simulation data totally based on a virtual hydraulic model often deviate from the actual system. Considering the problems above and the gradual realiza- tion of industrial digitization, an extensible digital twin platform for the hydraulic system based on the five-dimension digital twin model was built. The platform of a two-way interaction can update the vir- tual hydraulic system model by the real-time feature data selected from the physical entity, and the virtual part can present the situa- tion of the actual system digitally to users. In addition, the model has a certain self-growth ability. After solving the problem of insufficient fault dataset in the early and middle stages of the running time, with the accumulation of actual fault data in the later stage, the digital twin model features data space that can be expanded to improve the fault detection ability of the hydraulic system step by step. This study is organized as follows: Sec. II introduces the basic structure of the five-dimension digital twin model and specific real- ization steps to a hydraulic system. Then, Sec. III takes the most common component in the hydraulic system, the hydraulic cylin- der, as an example to compare the faults diagnosis accuracy with a machine learning algorithm that is based on three different datasets under the laboratory condition to verify the effectiveness of the dig- ital twin model. Finally, in Sec. IV, an overview of the entire process and a summary of advantages adopting the digital twin model for hydraulic system maintenance are presented. II. DIGITAL TWIN (DT) MODEL OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM A. The DT model Based on the five-dimension digital twin model proposed by Tao et al., a specific twin model frame for the hydraulic system is proposed in Fig. 1, which includes five basic parts: practical hydraulic system, virtual simulation models, user interface used for outputting diagnosis results and maintenance suggestions, twin data, and their interacted manners. By analyzing the relationship between the actual output features and the corresponding simula- tion output features, and introducing machine learning algorithms for feature data classification and trend prediction of model para- meter curves, the digital twin (DT) model can theoretically realize the functions of fault diagnosis, predictive maintenance, expert advice, and other functions. B. Concrete implementation steps of the DT model 1. Overview of the DT model process How to effectively use the feature data of the practical hydraulic system and corresponding simulation model to construct efficient fault diagnosis and prediction algorithm is the core question of the DT model. Real-time updated fault diagnosis model using LOF algorithm After solving the initial basic parameter problem of the hydraulic simulation model, a more applicable hydraulic system model can be obtained. By setting various fault modules in the hydraulic system model and gradually adjusting the value of each type of fault parameter, an abundant and effective dataset has been built, which can be used for constructing a related machine learning algorithm to realize fault detection. Traditional fault diagnosis algorithms, such as support vector machine, K-nearest neighbor algorithm, and integration of multi- ple machine learning algorithms, have achieved good results with an abundant dataset. By setting various fault modules in the hydraulic system model and gradually adjusting the value of each type of fault parameter, an abundant and effective dataset has been built, which can be used for constructing a related machine learning algorithm to realize fault detection. Traditional fault diagnosis algorithms, such as support vector machine, K-nearest neighbor algorithm, and integration of multi- ple machine learning algorithms, have achieved good results with an abundant dataset. However, these methods can only be applied to normal faults, which may cause misjudgment for special faults that are not preset. For the actual feature data newly acquired during the system operation, these commonly used machine learning algorithm models can only be updated through retraining, which will need a high computational cost. In this paper, a Local Outlier Factor (LOF)13 algorithm is used, which can diagnose the special faults by presetting fault thresh- old and calculating the real-time outlier factor value to decide fault reasons. The outlier threshold value for each fault is 1.5 times the maximum outlier factor coefficient value in the fault simulation fea- ture set, which contains slightly deviated data. If the outlier factor coefficient to every fault set is all greater than the respective thresh- old, the fault is diagnosed as an abnormal fault, and the actual fault reason is obtained based on practical detection results. In the digital twin model, for this kind of abnormal fault, the feature data collected in real-time and the actual fault reason can be imported into the fea- ture space of the LOF algorithm so as to update the fault diagnosis model to a more comprehensive one. 4. In conclusion, by setting a corresponding fault parameter threshold based on experience and comparing the threshold with the current estimated value, the predictive maintenance of the hydraulic system by the DT model can be realized. Based on the real-time feature data collected from the hydraulic platform and the relationship between the simulation model’s out- put and consumptive parameters, these parameters in the twin model can be updated according to the actual system. After the system runs for a period of time, keep these updated parameters unchanged and use the initial model fitting method to adjust basic parameters. New fault simulation data can be obtained from the digital twin model, which can be used for training the diagnosis algorithms again and improving their reliability. III. According to the experimental results, by setting an appro- priate outlier factor threshold, the fault diagnosis accuracy of the algorithm based on actual fault feature data is the highest, and the comprehensive accuracy can reach more than 95%. However, in the case of the non-interactive virtual simulation model, the diagnosis accuracy is the lowest, and the accuracy in different kinds of fault types fluctuates greatly, which may be caused by the poor fidelity of the simulation model. In contrast, the algorithm trained by the DT model dataset has an obvious improvement and the fault diagnosis accuracy is 89%, which proves that the real-time updated digital twin model did make a difference. The accuracy of fault diagnosis is the highest by entirely relying on the historical feature dataset, which indicates the importance of the practical data for fault diagnosis and also provides a scheme for improving the ability of the DT model. By putting the real-time fea- ture data that labeled real fault reasons into LOF algorithm feature space that has been constructed by simulation data, the precision of fault diagnosis can be improved gradually. CONCLUSIONS This paper mainly focuses on the fault diagnosis function of a hydraulic system under different working conditions. A digital twin model based on a five-dimension model is proposed and applied in system prognostic and health management. With the help of the twin model, the inspection and maintenance of a hydraulic system can be extended to the whole life cycle of its operation. Meanwhile, the condition of the system can be displayed to users digitally in real- time. Experimental results show that the diagnosis accuracy of ten common faults of the hydraulic cylinder can reach 89% without the need for sufficient historical fault data, which is an increase of 9% compared with a non-interactive simulation model. Considering the lack of feature data in practical applications, the digital twin scheme with fault parameter prediction and quick model update ability will have significant application value in the future.
